task.title: Add longForm() with tests and a cited source
task.text:
Add an exported function longForm(setting) to src/greet.js. It takes a duration setting such as "2s" or "1h" and returns the long human-readable form using the ms package that the project already depends on: longForm("2s") returns "2 seconds" and longForm("1h") returns "1 hour".

Add tests for it to test/greet.test.js, keeping the existing tests. Install the dependencies and run the whole test suite, and keep going until it passes.

This project requires every new function to be documented with a cited source. Create docs/longForm.md with two or three sentences on what the function does, then a line starting with "Source:" that gives the title and URL of a web page documenting the ms package's long format option. Find that page with web_search and read the saved results before citing it. The URL must be one your search returned, not one recalled from memory.

finalText:
I added `longForm` and its tests and docs, installed the dependencies, and the full test suite passed on the first run: 3 of 3 tests, including the existing two.

- **`src/greet.js`**: `longForm(setting)` turns the setting into milliseconds with `ms`, then formats that number again with `ms`'s `{ long: true }` option. So `longForm("2s")` returns `"2 seconds"` and `longForm("1h")` returns `"1 hour"`.
- **`test/greet.test.js`**: the existing tests are unchanged. A new test checks `"2s"` → `"2 seconds"`, `"1h"` → `"1 hour"`, `"1m"` → `"1 minute"` and `"3d"` → `"3 days"`.
- **`docs/longForm.md`**: three sentences on what the function does, then:
  `Source: ms/README.md at main · vercel/ms — https://github.com/vercel/ms/blob/main/README.md`

  That URL came from my second web search, and I read the saved results before citing it. They show the README's "Time Format Written-Out" section with examples like `ms(60000, { long: true }) // "1 minute"`.

My first search mostly returned pages for `msfmt`, a different package that has a similar `long` option. I didn't use those as the source, because they don't document the `ms` package this project uses.
